Even for sites that effectively weed out bots there is still extensive scalping - it's just done by live human beings. Event promoters want to ensure a predictable profit by limiting risk, so they sell tickets at below market rates to guarantee they sell 100% of their seats. Because these tickets are sold at below market rates, it's profitable for "scalpers" to buy the tickets and profit from the risk of trying to resell them at market rates.

TLDR: Scalping won't go away unless promoters raise prices to market rates, which is about what scalpers charge.

  • Or instead they secure purchases with ID like airlines do, so there's no point trading.

There is some of both. The servers can only handle so much traffic. The bots will intentionally flood the site and lock them up.

Follow with me. For simplicity sake let's say the servers are designed to handle 1000 connections/unique log ins. Groups of scalpers will use 10,000 computers to try and simultaneously login. The scalpers in essence flood in and they get 1000 connections. They will then use those 1000 connections to buy every ticket they can. This is often done in 20-100 ticket blocks quickly selling out the venue.

Picture you, sitting there on your laptop trying to get in. You try to log-in right at 10:01 when the market opens. Instead, the 10,000 computer guys has been cycling his computers with 1000 of them attempting to log in every 2-3 seconds so that at the exact moment it's open every available connection is in. You never had a shot. You just wanted 2 tickets for you and your buddy. Now you have to go to a 3rd party (the scalper) and pay extra + another fee back to the original ticket company.

Often, this is done by an out-of-the-country dealer in violation of local and sometimes federal law. There is a monopoly created.

Nothing will be done because the original ticket seller will often list the origin ticket price well below "market" value. However, the charge a small fee 5-10% on the first time it is sold. Then, they basically want the ticket to be sold as many times as possible collecting a 5-10% fee every time. In essence, they falsify their ticket prices.

This is not the same as some dude trying to unload a handful of tickets on craigslist or the street corner (which ironically is actually far more regulated), this is borderline monopoly and extortion.
